subject: Mid-cycle traction signal & asks — action required
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, cloudops-team@acmecloud.com, procurement@bluebridge.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-cycle traction signal & asks — action required

Team — attaching a short pulse for mid-cycle OKR status and a couple of targeted asks we need to resolve before QBR prep next week. TL;DR: two initiatives are at-risk (Edge cache rollout + Low-latency routing experiment). If we don’t close infra commitments and procurement timelines this sprint, we will need to re-scope impact targets.

Summary (see attached midcycle_pulse_deck.pdf):
- OKR: Reduce average 95th p99 latency by 20% — current: on-track (green) for hosted API, at-risk (amber) for dedicated/private in AP regions.
- OKR: Cost-per-token reduction 15% — green for batching & quantization experiments; amber for prefix-cache adoption (dependency: Edge rollout).
- Initiative: Edge cache rollout (owned: Karthik) — blockers: AcmeCloud regional capacity commitment + runbook completion.
- Initiative: Low-latency routing experiment (owned: Engineering) — partially blocked by missing canary traffic window and expanded tracing config.

Asks (we need answers by EOD Friday, 2026-10-08):
1) Cloud capacity: Acme Ops — can you confirm regional GPU pool availability for us (us-west-2) for the week of 10/19? If not, propose fallback region and expected perf delta. (cc: cloudops-team@acmecloud.com)
2) Procurement: BlueBridge — can we get an estimated PO issuance date for the Dedicated commitment (SOW #RB-2026-09)? We need the PO before 10/15 to hit procurement gating.
3) Engineering: Karthik — please rebaseline the Edge rollout milestones in OKRs sheet (attached okrs_table.xlsx) and call out any scope you want to pull to Q4 to preserve impact on cost-per-token.
4) Product/Leadership: Markus/Vanessa/Naomi — decision required: if (1) or (2) slips beyond dates above, do we accept an amber impact on the latency OKR or do we pull the prefix-cache work into a narrower scope with reduced throughput targets?

Attachments: midcycle_pulse_deck.pdf, okrs_table.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
- Quick sync (15 min) Friday 10/08 10:00am PT to confirm decisions and surface any hard blockers.
- If procurement/capacity commit fails, engineering and product agree a narrowed scope within 48 hours and notify stakeholders.

Thanks — short and actionable please.

—
Aditya Rao
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle traction signal & asks — action required

Aditya — thanks for the clear summary. Quick reactions:
- I agree we should not let two big infra dependencies threaten both latency and cost targets. If Acme can’t commit to us-west-2 capacity for the 10/19 window, we should accept a narrower latency target (p99 down 12–15% vs 20%) and focus on prefix-cache rollout for hosted only.
- Karthik: please surface a one-page decision matrix (cost vs impact vs risk) by Thursday COB so leadership can choose a path at the Friday sync.

If possible, avoid pulling work that reduces throughput; instead prefer scope that reduces integration surface.

On procurement: Naomi, can you confirm we have any exceptions available to accelerate PO issuance if we agree to a targeted scope change?

—Markus

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, cloudops-team@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-10-05T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle traction signal & asks — action required

Looping in a couple more specifics to make the Friday decision as clean as possible.

Dependency map (short):
- Acme capacity (critical) — affects Edge cache rollout and full-region routing experiments. If Acme gives a partial window (e.g., 10/19–10/21), we can stage rollout to a subset of prefixes and preserve an early impact signal.
- Runbook & SRE playbook (engineering deliverable) — need a vetted runbook + post-deploy rollback plan before we can escalate to canary traffic. See attached deployment_runbook.md (draft).
- DocuSign/SOW gating — procurement needs the signed SOW to start invoicing and reserve capacity. Link to SOW: https://docusign.com/12345abcde

Immediate asks: 
- Karthik: update the OKR sheet to mark which work can be staged (prefix subset) vs requires full rollout. Add per-item risk and estimated rollback effort.
- CloudOps (Acme): if you can confirm a partial window, flag any networking limitations (e.g., no inbound SNAT) that would change our routing plan.
- Naomi/Procurement: if PO can be targeted for partial scope, please advise timeline.

If we have answers by EOD Thursday 10/08, Friday’s 15-min will be strictly decision-focused. Otherwise we’ll convert the slot to a 45-min remediation working session.

Thanks,
—Vanessa
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Quick update from procurement and legal: we can prioritize the SOW review and aim to issue a preliminary PO for the partial scope by 10/14 provided we have the signed SOW and an explicit list of endpoints/regions. Two notes:
1) Legal needs the exact SOW appendix callout for region and expected traffic profile (small paragraph) — can Karthik/Eng supply by EOD Wednesday 10/07?
2) BlueBridge (procurement partner) noted they can fast-track to a provisional PO if leadership signs off on limited scope. That will reserve capacity on Acme’s side while full paperwork completes.

I’m available for a 10-min huddle after your decision on Friday.

—Naomi Feldman
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
